subject: Social Science

source.title: Social Science, Subject Code 087, Class X (2026-27)

internalBreakdown.component: Subject Enrichment Activity (project on Consumer Rights / Social Issues / Sustainable Development)

textbooks: India and the Contemporary World - II (NCERT, History)
Together, towards a safer India - Part III (CBSE, Disaster Management)
notes: Map work carries 5 marks of the 80 (History 2, Geography 3), counted inside the History and Geography unit marks.
An interdisciplinary project links History ch. 3, Geography ch. 7 and Economics ch. 4; it is internally assessed for 5 marks.

units.name: History: India and the Contemporary World - II

chapters.name: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
topics: The French Revolution and the making of nation states
Causes of the First World War
outcomes: Infers the impact of the French Revolution on European nation-making
Analyses the evolution of nationalism
Evaluates the reasons that led to the First World War

chapters.name: Nationalism in India
outcomes: Illustrates facets of nationalist movements
Evaluates the strategies of Gandhiji and other leaders
Summarises the effects of the First World War on Indian movements
notes: Map: Congress sessions 1920 Calcutta, 1920 Nagpur, 1927 Madras; satyagrahas at Kheda, Champaran, Ahmedabad mill workers; Jallianwala Bagh; Dandi March

chapters.name: The Making of a Global World
topics: The pre-modern world (board examination: subtopics 1 to 1.3, pre-modern world to conquest, disease and trade)
Rebuilding the world economy: the post-war era (internal project)
outcomes: Summarises changes that transformed the world
Depicts global interconnectedness from pre-modern times to the present
Enumerates the impact of colonialism on the livelihoods of colonised people
notes: Only subtopics 1 to 1.3 are evaluated in the board examination; subtopics 2 to 4.4 are assessed through the interdisciplinary project

chapters.name: The Age of Industrialisation
topics: Industrialisation in the colonies, with focus on India
outcomes: Enumerates economic, political and social features of pre- and post-industrialisation
Analyses the impact of industrialisation on colonies
notes: Assessed as part of Periodic Assessment only

chapters.name: Print Culture and the Modern World
topics: Print from East Asia to Europe and India
The print revolution and its impact
outcomes: Traces the development of print
Compares manuscript and print traditions
Summarises the impact of the print revolution

chapters.name: Resources and Development
topics: Resource planning and development in India
outcomes: Justifies resource planning
Analyses data on non-optimal land use
Suggests measures for optimal use of under-utilised resources

chapters.name: Forest and Wildlife Resources
topics: Impact of grazing, wood cutting and developmental works
outcomes: Examines the importance of conserving forests and wildlife
Summarises reasons for biodiversity conservation

chapters.name: Water Resources
outcomes: Examines reasons for water conservation
Analyses how multipurpose projects meet water needs
notes: Map: Salal, Bhakra Nangal, Tehri, Rana Pratap Sagar, Sardar Sarovar, Hirakud, Nagarjuna Sagar, Tungabhadra

chapters.name: Agriculture
topics: Role of agriculture in the economy and society
Types of farming and crop production
outcomes: Examines the role of agriculture
Analyses challenges faced by the farming community
notes: Map: major rice and wheat areas; largest producer states of sugarcane, tea, coffee, rubber, cotton and jute

chapters.name: Minerals and Energy Resources
topics: Iron ore mines, coal mines and oil fields (map)
notes: The document repeats the Manufacturing Industries learning outcomes for this chapter, so no chapter-specific outcomes are recorded
Map: iron ore, coal and oil fields; thermal and nuclear power plants

chapters.name: Manufacturing Industries
outcomes: Differentiates types of manufacturing industries and their significance
Analyses the relation between raw materials and industrial location
Develops strategies for sustainable manufacturing
notes: Map: cotton textile industries, iron and steel plants, software technology parks (locating and labelling only)

chapters.name: Lifelines of National Economy
topics: Interdisciplinary project with History ch. 3 and Economics ch. 4
Major sea ports and international airports (map)
outcomes: See Annexure III-B of the source document
notes: Only map pointing is evaluated in the board examination; the chapter is otherwise part of the interdisciplinary project

chapters.name: Power-sharing
topics: Need for power sharing in democracy
Power sharing in Belgium and Sri Lanka
Power sharing in preserving unity and stability
outcomes: Enumerates the need for power sharing
Compares power sharing in India, Sri Lanka and Belgium

chapters.name: Federalism
topics: Policies and politics that strengthened federalism
outcomes: Infers how federalism is practised in India
Analyses what has strengthened federalism

chapters.name: Gender, Religion and Caste
topics: Gender, religion and caste in the practice of democracy
outcomes: Examines the role of gender, religion and caste in democracy
Analyses whether expressions of difference are healthy for democracy

chapters.name: Political Parties
topics: Role, purpose and number of political parties
Right to vote and citizens' duties
outcomes: Understands the electoral process for parties
Examines the role of political parties in democracy

chapters.name: Outcomes of Democracy
topics: Quality of government, economic well-being, inequality, social differences, conflict, freedom and dignity
outcomes: Enumerates what the success of democracy depends on

chapters.name: Development
outcomes: Examines processes in setting developmental goals
Analyses what per capita income shows
Compares per capita incomes of countries

chapters.name: Sectors of the Indian Economy
topics: Economic activities in different sectors and their contribution to growth
Organised and unorganised sectors and employment
outcomes: Analyses how sectors contribute to growth
Summarises employment in organised and unorganised sectors
Explains the roles of public and private sectors

chapters.name: Money and Credit
topics: Money as a medium of exchange
outcomes: Explains money as a medium of exchange
Analyses sources of credit
Summarises the role of self-help groups

chapters.name: Globalisation and the Indian Economy
topics: Factors that have enabled globalisation (board examination)
The struggle for a fair globalisation (internal project)
outcomes: Explains the concept and impact of globalisation
Evaluates the drivers of globalisation
Explains the role of the G20 and India's place in it
notes: Only 'What is globalisation?' and 'Factors that have enabled globalisation' are evaluated in the board examination

chapters.name: Consumer Rights
topics: Project work: Consumer Rights OR Social Issues OR Sustainable Development
outcomes: See Annexure III of the source document
notes: Project work, assessed internally as the Subject Enrichment Activity
